# E032 -- Harvard University Graphic Identity Guidelines

- **Industry:** Education
- **Year:** 2021
- **Source file:** harvard-2021-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 51
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "Graphic Identity Guidelines" -- developed by Harvard Public Affairs & Communications, September 2021
- Purpose: establish and maintain clear, unified University identity within the Harvard community and beyond
- Primarily for Central Administration and Faculty of Arts and Sciences departments
- Goals: improve consistency and reduce costs from units developing their own marks
- Contact: identityguidelines@harvard.edu

## Logo
- Identity system built around the Veritas Shield and University Signature (wordmark + shield)
- Key elements: Veritas Shield, University Signature, Signature Elements, University Seal
- General rules:
  - Use original artwork in provided format; never manually alter
  - Treat signature as artwork; do not typeset the Harvard wordmark
  - Always use shield alongside wordmark; never use wordmark without shield
  - Scale proportionally; never stretch
  - Give signature its own space; avoid crowding with other elements
  - Do not outline the shield or use in reverse
  - Keep primary extensions to one line; do not stack
- Adorned Veritas Shield (with wreath and banner) restricted to commemorative/official University purposes and senior-level leadership offices (President, Provost) -- requires permission

## Typography
- Dedicated typography section referenced in TOC -- not covered in sampled pages

## Color
- Harvard Crimson: PMS 187U / PMS 1807C / CMYK C7-M94-Y65-K25 / HEX #A51C30 / RGB 165-28-48
- Black: PMS Process Black U/C / CMYK 0-0-0-100 / HEX #1E1E1E / RGB 30-30-30
- Shield should not be applied against a crimson background
- Pantone values serve as starting point -- proof against printed chip and adjust

## Graphics
- Veritas Shield is the primary graphic element
- Shield must remain in original form (crimson, black, white)
- Greyscale (50% black) version available when color reproduction is not possible

## Outliers
- Permission-gated usage of the Adorned Shield -- reflects institutional hierarchy and governance
- Extremely specific color values with both coated and uncoated Pantone specs
- Shield-centric identity system where the symbol is more important than the wordmark (wordmark cannot appear without shield)
- Cost reduction mentioned as an explicit goal -- unusual pragmatic framing for an Ivy League institution

## Quality Score
- **Score: 3/5** -- Well-structured graphic identity manual with comprehensive logo usage rules, precise color specifications, and clear governance. Covers the essentials for a university identity system. However, it is narrowly focused on graphic identity rather than a full brand guide -- no tone of voice, brand strategy, or positioning content. Typography and photography sections exist but were not in sampled pages.
